title: Bulbs in a row
body: Here the bulbs sit one after the other in one loop. Scientists call this a series circuit. There's only one path, so the same flow goes through every bulb.
A bulb doesn't use up the flow. It uses the flow's energy to make light and heat. Think of a water wheel in a stream. The wheel takes energy from the water, but all the water flows on.
Each bulb you add is like another narrow bit of pipe. Less flows round the whole loop, so all the bulbs dim together. Two bulbs that are exactly alike always glow the same.
equation: flow through bulb A = flow through bulb B
realWorld: Some strings of fairy lights are wired in a row like this. If one bulb breaks, the loop opens. Then the whole string goes dark.
sources: OpenStax College Physics 2e, §21.1 Resistors in Series and Parallel. https://openstax.org/books/college-physics-2e/pages/21-1-resistors-in-series-and-parallel
